content.question: In K-fold cross-validation, how is the model trained and validated?
options: The model is trained on K − 1 folds and validated on the remaining one; this is repeated K times, so each fold serves as the validation set exactly once.
The model is trained on one fold and validated on the other K − 1 folds in a single pass.
The model is trained on all K folds at once and validated on a separate hold-out set.
The model is trained on half of the data and validated on the other half, once.
content.answer: The model is trained on K − 1 folds and validated on the remaining one; this is repeated K times, so each fold serves as the validation set exactly once.
